name: Germany
tagline: No tuition, but your IB subject choice decides everything
summary: Germany is the one country in Europe where a single written rule decides whether your IB Diploma counts at all, and it is about which six subjects you took, not how many points you scored. Get the combination right and public universities cost you a semester contribution of roughly 70-430 EUR and nothing else. Get it wrong and you are limited to certain fields or shut out entirely. Most bachelor's degrees are still taught in German; English-taught bachelor's exist but are a minority, concentrated in universities of applied sciences and private business schools.
whyConsider: No tuition fees at public universities for EU/EEA students - you pay only a semester contribution, usually including a public transport pass.
Ikast-Brande Gymnasium is named in Annex 1 of the KMK IB agreement, which removes the Maths SL penalty that blocks most IB students from STEM subjects in Germany.
Very large system: hundreds of universities and Fachhochschulen, so there is almost always somewhere that teaches your subject.
Strong engineering, natural sciences and economics, with close links to industry and paid internship semesters at applied-sciences universities.
Living costs outside Munich, Frankfurt and Hamburg are low by Northern European standards.
watchOuts: The KMK subject-combination rule is absolute. If your six IB subjects do not match it, no amount of points will fix it.
Taking Mathematics AA SL or AI SL normally restricts you to non-STEM subjects - unless your school is on the KMK Annex 1 list (Ikast-Brande and Grenaa are).
English-taught bachelor's are the exception, not the rule. Many attractive programmes require German at C1/DSH level.
Baden-Wurttemberg (Heidelberg, Freiburg, Karlsruhe, Stuttgart, Tubingen, Mannheim, Konstanz) charges non-EU students 1,500 EUR per semester. EU citizens are exempt.
Popular subjects have a Numerus Clausus: places are rationed by grade, and your converted German grade is what you are ranked on.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: 24 points (a full IB Diploma). Each of the six required subjects must be graded at least 4. If exactly one subject is a 3, it can be compensated by a grade of at least 5 in another subject at the same or a higher level, provided the total is at least 24 points.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: KMK agreement of 10.03.1986 in the version of 15.06.2023, section 1. Among your six IB subjects there must be: (1) two languages at level A or B, of which at least one is a continued foreign language taken as Language A or Language B HL; (2) a natural science (Biology, Chemistry or Physics); (3) Mathematics (Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation); (4) a social science (History, Geography, Economics, Psychology, Social Anthropology, Business and Management or Global Politics). The sixth subject may be another of those, or: Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, Film, Literature and Performance, a further modern foreign language, Latin, Classical Greek, General Chemistry, Applied Chemistry, Environmental Systems and Societies, Computer Science, Design Technology, World Religions, Sports Exercise and Health Science, or Digital Society. From the May 2025 session onwards, at least one of your three Higher Level subjects must be a language, Mathematics or a natural science (section 1b). All six subjects must have been taken across the full two years of the Diploma Programme.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: The KMK sets one formula for the whole country: N = 1 + 3 x (Pmax - P) / (Pmax - Pmin), where P is your IB total including bonus points, Pmax = 42 and Pmin = 24. Any total from 42 to 45 points is set equal to the top German grade 1.0. Worked examples from that formula: 42+ points = 1.0; 40 = 1.3; 38 = 1.7; 36 = 2.0; 34 = 2.3; 30 = 3.0; 24 = 4.0.
notes: Mathematics at Standard Level is the single biggest trap. Under footnote 3 of the agreement, anyone presenting Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL from the May 2021 session onwards can normally only be given a subject-restricted university entrance (fachgebundene Hochschulzugangsberechtigung) for subjects outside maths, science and technology.

There is a written exception, and Denmark is in it. Annex 1 of the agreement (version of 26.03.2026) lists Ikast-Brande Gymnasium (school code 004672, valid from the May 2022 session) and Grenaa Gymnasium (001488, from May 2025). Graduates of these schools are treated as meeting the mathematics requirement even with Maths SL, so they get the general Hochschulzugangsberechtigung.
The Diploma must have been earned after at least twelve consecutive years of full-time schooling.
German citizens who did not take German in the IB programme must prove sufficient German before starting a degree in Germany; the detail is set by each federal state.

If your combination does not satisfy section 1, the fallback is the Feststellungspruefung at a Studienkolleg, or one successfully completed year of university study in a country whose leaving certificate gives direct access to German universities.
Course Results (certificates without the full Diploma) are not covered by the agreement.

portal.name: hochschulstart.de (medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, pharmacy) and uni-assist or the university's own portal for everything else

deadlines.label: Medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and pharmacy - applicants whose leaving certificate is dated after 15 January of the application year (this is you)
deadlines.year: 2026 entry - dates for 2027 entry not yet published
deadlines.notes: hochschulstart.de published 15.07.2026 as the exclusion deadline for winter semester 2026/27. Your IB results arrive 5-6 July 2027, so you fall in the Neuabiturient group and this is the deadline that matters. Re-check the exact 2027 date on hochschulstart.de from spring 2027.

deadlines.label: Medicine group - applicants whose leaving certificate predates 16 January of the application year (a gap-year applicant)
deadlines.year: 2026 entry - dates for 2027 entry not yet published
deadlines.notes: If you take a gap year and apply with your 2027 certificate for 2028 entry, you become an Altabiturient and the deadline moves forward by six weeks.

deadlines.label: DoSV application phase opens
deadlines.year: 2026 entry - dates for 2027 entry not yet published
deadlines.notes: The coordination phase for the centrally allocated subjects started 16.07.2026 for winter 2026/27.

deadlines.label: Most other bachelor's programmes, winter semester
deadlines.year: Typical deadline - each university sets its own, and some English-taught programmes close as early as January
deadlines.notes: Always take the deadline from the programme page, not from a general guide. Programmes with selection procedures or English-language entry often close months earlier.

deadlines.label: uni-assist preliminary review (VPD) - submit well before the university deadline
deadlines.notes: uni-assist states evaluation usually takes 4 to 6 weeks after you submit the online form, and Western European applications are quoted at 3-4 weeks. With IB results on 5-6 July and a 15 July university deadline, this is genuinely tight - start the uni-assist file in spring 2027 with your predicted grades and school documents.

steps: From autumn 2026, check each programme you like against the KMK subject rule above - do this before anything else, because it cannot be fixed later.
Check on anabin (anabin.kmk.org) or with the university whether your Diploma is treated as a general or subject-restricted entrance qualification.
Find out for each university whether it takes applications directly or through uni-assist, and whether the programme is taught in German or English.
If German is required, get the certificate (DSH, TestDaF or equivalent) organised in good time - this is usually the thing that makes people miss a year.
Open your uni-assist or university account in spring 2027, upload school documents and predicted grades, and pay the handling fee.
For medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or pharmacy, register on hochschulstart.de and submit by the July deadline.
Send the final IB Diploma as soon as it arrives in early July 2027, then enrol and pay the semester contribution before the semester starts in October.
application.selectionNotes: Many programmes are open admission (zulassungsfrei): meet the requirements and you are in. Others carry a local Numerus Clausus, where places are ranked by your converted German grade. Medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and pharmacy are restricted nationwide and allocated centrally through hochschulstart.de. Applicants with a foreign leaving certificate are often handled in a separate quota with its own place count, which can work either for or against you.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: A real but limited option. Most public universities teach bachelor's in German; English-taught bachelor's cluster at universities of applied sciences (such as Rhine-Waal), a few public programmes (University College Freiburg's Liberal Arts and Sciences) and private institutions. Search the DAAD International Programmes database and filter for Bachelor + English.
language.englishProof: For English-taught programmes, IB English A (Literature or Language and Literature) is normally accepted; English B HL is often accepted too but is decided programme by programme. Otherwise IELTS or TOEFL. Exact requirement not verified centrally - check each programme page.
notes: For German-taught degrees you normally need DSH-2 or TestDaF 4x4 (roughly C1). Four years of German B in the IB is not automatically enough.
German citizens who studied abroad without German in the IB must prove German knowledge before enrolling, under section 1e of the KMK agreement.
Even on an English-taught degree, everyday life, part-time work and housing searches happen in German.

tuitionEuEea.value: No tuition at public universities. You pay a semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) of roughly 70-430 EUR per semester, which usually includes a local or regional transport ticket. Example: University of Hamburg charged 402 EUR for winter semester 2026/27.

tuitionNonEu.value: Also free at most public universities, with one big exception: Baden-Wurttemberg charges non-EU/EEA students 1,500 EUR per semester, plus the normal semester contribution. Students with a German school-leaving qualification are exempt. Some other states have debated similar fees.

livingCostMonthly.value: About 876 EUR per month on average (2023 social survey), with 900-1,200 EUR realistic depending on the city. Non-EU students must show 992 EUR per month in a blocked account for a student visa.
livingCostMonthly.year: 2023 survey figure, visa figure from 1 January 2025

notes: uni-assist charges a handling fee per application and for a VPD. The amount could not be confirmed from an official uni-assist page during this research - check uni-assist.de before budgeting.
The semester contribution is not tuition. It funds the Studierendenwerk, the student body and, at most universities, a transport pass.
Munich, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Cologne and Stuttgart are markedly more expensive than Leipzig, Dresden, Bochum or Kiel.

funding: Danish SU can in many cases be taken abroad for a full degree - check the rules with SU Styrelsen before you commit, because this is usually the largest single source of money.
Deutschlandstipendium: merit-based scholarships awarded by individual German universities; you apply to the university, not centrally.
BAfoeg (German state study support) is open to some EU citizens, typically where you or a parent have worked or lived in Germany; it is not automatic for a newly arrived EU student.
DAAD scholarship database: mostly master's and research level, but worth searching.
Erasmus+ only helps once you are enrolled and want to spend a period elsewhere.
workRights: As a Danish (EU) citizen you have full access to the German labour market with no permit and no hour limit - you are only limited by tax and social-insurance thresholds for student jobs. Non-EU students on a residence permit under section 16b of the Residence Act may work 140 full days or 280 half days per calendar year, or alternatively up to 20 hours a week during the lecture period, a rule in force since 1 March 2024. Source: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/aufenthg_2004/__16b.html
residency: EU citizens do not need a visa or residence permit. You register your address (Anmeldung) at the local Buergeramt or Einwohnermeldeamt shortly after moving in, which gets you a tax ID and is needed to open a bank account and enrol. Non-EU students apply for a national student visa at the German embassy before travelling and then convert it into a residence permit at the local Auslaenderbehoerde.
housing: Student halls are run by the regional Studierendenwerk and are the cheapest option, but demand far exceeds supply in Munich, Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg, Berlin and Stuttgart. Apply to the Studierendenwerk as soon as you have an offer, and search shared flats (WG) in parallel on wg-gesucht.de. In the big cities expect a hunt of several weeks and be ready to start the semester in temporary accommodation.
healthcare: Health insurance is compulsory and you cannot enrol without proof of it. As an EU student with a Danish EHIC you can usually apply to a German statutory insurer for an exemption (Befreiung), which they confirm electronically to the university - do this before enrolment day. If you take a job in Germany or your EHIC does not cover you, you join German statutory student insurance instead, which costs around 120-140 EUR a month including long-term care insurance; confirm the current rate with the insurer.

institutions.name: Technical University of Munich
institutions.note: Germany's strongest technical university and the obvious target for an IB student with HL Maths and Physics; check language of instruction per programme, as several bachelor's are German-taught.

institutions.name: RWTH Aachen University
institutions.note: Huge engineering school close to the Dutch and Belgian borders; bachelor's teaching is mostly in German, with English arriving at master's level.

institutions.name: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
institutions.note: Germany's best-known general university; bachelor's are almost entirely in German, so treat it as a German-language destination.

institutions.name: Heidelberg University
institutions.note: Germany's oldest university and a research heavyweight; note that Baden-Wurttemberg's 1,500 EUR per semester non-EU fee applies here.

institutions.name: University of Freiburg - University College Freiburg
institutions.englishBachelors: Liberal Arts and Sciences BA/BSc, taught in English - described as the first English-language liberal arts degree at a German public university.
institutions.note: The closest thing Germany has to a Dutch-style English-taught liberal arts college inside a big public research university; small cohort and selective.

institutions.name: Rhine-Waal University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: A large share of its bachelor's degrees are taught entirely in English, across engineering, life sciences, society and economics.
institutions.note: Public, so no tuition - only the semester contribution - and one of the few German institutions where you can do a full English-taught bachelor's on the state system.

institutions.name: Constructor University
institutions.englishBachelors: All bachelor's taught in English, on a residential international campus.
institutions.note: Private and fee-paying, but the most fully international English-taught campus in Germany; scholarships are common, so ask about the net price rather than the sticker price.

institutions.name: University of Mannheim
institutions.note: Germany's leading business and social science university, run on a baroque palace campus and on a semester calendar closer to the English-speaking world.

institutions.name: Free University of Berlin
institutions.note: Strong in the humanities and social sciences and deeply international at graduate level, but bachelor's teaching is in German.

institutions.name: Technical University of Berlin
institutions.note: A large technical university in the middle of Berlin; cheap by capital-city standards but the housing market is the hardest part.

institutions.name: Bard College Berlin
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught liberal arts bachelor's, awarded as both a German BA and a US BA.
institutions.note: Tiny English-language liberal arts college in Pankow; seminar-based and essay-heavy, which suits students coming out of TOK and the Extended Essay.

institutions.name: Frankfurt School of Finance & Management
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught bachelor's in business and finance.
institutions.note: Private and expensive, but plugged directly into the Frankfurt banking market; check the fee and the scholarship scheme before applying.

institutions.name: WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor in International Business Administration, taught in English.
institutions.note: Small, selective private business school on the Rhine with a strong start-up alumni network; entry involves its own selection process, not just grades.

institutions.name: Leuphana University Luneburg
institutions.note: Runs a US-style college model with a major/minor structure, including an individually designed bachelor's; an hour from Hamburg.
